original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: For real factorizations of 2I_8 by E8 root normals, prove the label-pairing copy cost is exactly 9 per nonzero term, hence at least 81 for nine or more terms; after deleting at most 13 lines the cost is at least 9t-p. Rank-9 excursions and E-graph rank above 8 stay outside the floor.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a block-climb profile beating the selected word by at least 5 percent. The decoder scope map leaves the copy bill of nine or more costly rank-8 terms undetermined, which is the overcomplete branch of that question. This package prices only the factor-rank-(8, 8) branch and shows it cannot undercut the eight-term floor. It does not produce a per-call profile or a kappa improvement.
bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are a large part of recursive cost, so a factorization that delivered the same rank-8 mass at lower copy cost would matter. Inside factor rank 8 the copy bill is exactly 9 per term, above the eight-term floor once nine or more terms are used. Any saving on this identity has to leave the root span. This is a side obstruction, not a new supplier.
stop_rule: Stop when the rank-(8, 8) bill is proved for every term count and a rank-9 control shows the hypothesis is necessary. Do not search this class for a word that beats the selected kappa.
evidence: research/nine-costly-rank8-copy-floor/PROOF.md and verify.py. P120 rank-(8, 8) cost is 9t (witnesses 72 and 81). Any deletion of at most 13 lines costs at least 9t-p (frame-puncture witness 79). A rank-9 excursion costs 80 and drops one term to 8. No selected-frontier edit.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Can a real factorization of 2G with at least one factor rank greater than 8 have label-pairing copy cost below 72?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem 3 gives 9t only while both factors stay in the root span. The ten-term rank-(9, 9) example meets 72, and the rank-9 excursion in verify.py only reaches 80, so this is the smallest remaining way for extra terms to undercut the eight-term floor.
open_questions.first_step: Start from the explicit excursion in verify.py, section excursion_control, or from the ten-term factorization in research/ten-term-copy-cost, and either drive the measured copy cost under 72 or isolate a defect budget that forbids it.
open_questions.blocked_by: No normal form is known once a factor column leaves the eight-dimensional root span. This package does not supply one.

open_questions.question: Can a real E-graph solution of rank at least 9 on P120 or on a frame complement have costly-term copy cost below the eight-term floor?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR1212 Theorem 1, which this corollary cites, stops at rank 8. A rank-9 E-graph solution is the other half of the scope-map gap and is not priced by Theorems 3 or 4.
open_questions.first_step: Write one exact real rank-9 solution of the E-graph equations on P120 and compute the label-pairing costs of its costly terms.
open_questions.blocked_by: There is no gauge form for rank >= 9. Finding a solution is a new search, not a computation inside this census.
